rows.text: Cascade is free mana, but this deck treats it as something better: a trigger. Half the cards here pay you specifically for casting spells FROM EXILE or for casting enormous creature spells, so a Maelstrom Wanderer that flips into two seven-drops is not just eighteen mana of value — it is a copy, a pile of damage and three cards on top. Build the mana, cast one big thing, and the rest happens on its own.

guide.title: The commander and the cascade chain

rows.name: Maelstrom Wanderer
rows.text: eight mana for two cascades and permanent haste for your whole board. The haste is not a rider — it is what lets the creatures you cascade into attack the same turn.

rows.name: Apex Devastator
rows.text: four cascades on one card. It is the single biggest turn in the deck.

rows.name: Imoti, Celebrant of Bounty
rows.text: every spell you cast with mana value six or more gains cascade. Half this deck qualifies.

rows.name: Quandrix, the Proof
rows.text: your instants and sorceries from hand gain cascade too, and it cascades itself.

rows.name: Averna, the Chaos Bloom
rows.text: every cascade also puts a land onto the battlefield. It ramps you while it digs.

rows.name: Etherium-Horn Sorcerer
rows.text: cascades, and it bounces itself to hand to cascade again.

rows.name: Aurora Phoenix
rows.text: cascades, and it climbs out of the graveyard every time you cast another cascade spell.

rows.name: Natural Reclamation
rows.text: removal with a cascade attached.

rows.name: Call Forth the Tempest
rows.text: two cascades and a sweeper scaled to everything you cast this turn.
Remember the rule: cascade finds the first nonland card with a LOWER mana value. This deck is deliberately top-heavy so the flips are big — Maelstrom Wanderer at eight can hit anything up to seven.

guide.title: Getting paid for casting from exile

rows.name: Nalfeshnee
rows.text: every spell you cast from exile is COPIED. With cascade, that is two of everything you flip into.

rows.name: Keeper of Secrets
rows.text: damage equal to the mana value of every spell you cast from anywhere but your hand. A double cascade into two big spells is a dozen damage.

rows.name: Passionate Archaeologist
rows.text: the same trigger stapled to your commander, and it hits every time.

rows.name: Improvisation Capstone
rows.text: free spells now, and paradigm makes it repeat at the beginning of every one of your main phases for the rest of the game.

rows.name: Creative Technique
rows.text: a free spell off the top, and demonstrate lets you copy it for a friend to keep the table happy.

rows.name: Sunbird's Invocation
rows.text: every spell you cast from HAND reveals its mana value in cards and casts a free one from among them. It turns each hard cast into two spells.

guide.title: Getting paid for casting big creatures

rows.name: Kozilek's Unsealing
rows.text: draw three for every creature spell of mana value seven or more, and two mana Spawn for every four-, five- or six-drop. It fuels itself.

rows.name: Sarkhan's Unsealing
rows.text: four damage to any target for mid-sized creatures, and four to EACH opponent and each of their creatures and planeswalkers for anything with power seven or more. Two big flips is a wrath and eight damage to the table.

rows.name: Monstrous Vortex
rows.text: every creature spell with power five or more discovers X. Another free spell on top of the cascade.

rows.name: Echoes of Eternity
rows.text: colourless spells you cast are copied, and colourless triggered abilities happen twice. With the Eldrazi package it doubles everything.

guide.title: The things you want to hit

rows.name: Kozilek, Butcher of Truth
rows.text: four cards on cast and annihilator 4.

rows.name: Artisan of Kozilek
rows.text: reanimates something on cast and annihilator 2.

rows.name: Etali, Primal Storm
rows.text: a free spell off every player's library on every attack, and it has haste from your commander.

rows.name: Etali, Primal Conqueror
rows.text: a free spell from every player on entry, and a flipped infect finisher later.

rows.name: Emrakul, the Promised End
rows.text: cheaper for every card type in your graveyard, and it takes over an opponent's whole turn.

rows.name: Decimator of the Provinces
rows.text: emerge makes it castable off a spare body, and it pumps and tramples the entire board for the kill.

rows.name: Elder Deep-Fiend
rows.text: flash, emerge, and it taps four permanents — a fog, a counterspell substitute, or the clear for a lethal attack.

rows.name: Ancient Silver Dragon
rows.text: an average of ten cards on connection.

rows.name: Ancient Copper Dragon
rows.text: an average of ten Treasures.

rows.name: Delina, Wild Mage
rows.text: token copies of whatever monster you just cascaded into, sometimes several.

rows.name: Genesis Ultimatum
rows.text: five cards deep, every permanent among them onto the battlefield.

rows.name: Selvala's Stampede
rows.text: the table votes, and both outcomes put your fatties into play.

rows.name: Sol Ring
rows.text: turn one.

rows.name: Mana Vault
rows.text: three on turn one.

rows.name: Thran Dynamo
rows.text: three more.

rows.name: Nature's Lore
rows.text: an untapped dual.

rows.name: Three Visits
rows.text: the second copy.

rows.name: Skyshroud Claim
rows.text: two untapped Forests, a four-mana swing.

rows.name: Farseek
rows.text: fetches a shockland.

rows.name: Cultivate
rows.text: a land now and a land in hand.

rows.name: Kodama's Reach
rows.text: the same.

rows.name: Rampant Growth
rows.text: the cheap one.

rows.name: Fellwar Stone
rows.text: two mana that usually taps for what you need.

rows.name: Talisman of Curiosity
rows.text: and the rest of the rocks. Getting to eight mana on turn five is the entire early game.

rows.name: Mana Drain
rows.text: counter their answer, and the mana casts a fatty next turn.

rows.name: An Offer You Can't Refuse
rows.text: one mana for anything noncreature.

rows.name: Beast Within
rows.text: instant-speed answer to any permanent.

rows.name: Chaos Warp
rows.text: the enchantment and planeswalker answer.

rows.name: Chaos Mutation
rows.text: exiles a creature from each player and replaces it with a random one — usually a downgrade for them and an upgrade for you.

rows.name: Natural Reclamation
rows.text: artifact or enchantment plus a cascade.

rows.name: Possibility Storm
rows.text: a lock that hurts everyone, but you have Nalfeshnee, Keeper of Secrets and Passionate Archaeologist to profit from every random cast. Deploy it against a combo table, not a creature one.

rows.name: The One Ring
rows.text: a turn of complete protection and then a growing draw engine.

rows.name: Rhystic Study
rows.text: their turns pay for your eight-drops.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep ramp. Two rocks and a land-fetch beats a hand of eight-drops every single time — the deck's payoff cards are all free once you can cast one big thing.

Cast the cascade spell BEFORE the value engines when you are behind, and after them when you are ahead. Nalfeshnee, Keeper of Secrets and Sarkhan's Unsealing turn one Maelstrom Wanderer into a lethal turn; without them it is just a big body.

rows.name: Averna, the Chaos Bloom
rows.text: three mana, and every cascade afterwards ramps you. She is much better on turn three than on turn eight.

rows.name: Maelstrom Wanderer
rows.text: he gives your whole board haste permanently, so the creatures you cascade into attack immediately. Do not forget the attack — half the deck's damage comes from monsters that arrived this turn.
